hints: A tree has no loops. Adding one cable creates exactly one loop. If you add the cables one by one, at which moment does the loop appear?

Union-find (disjoint set): add cables in order, joining their two ends. The first cable whose ends are already in the same set closes the loop — that is the answer (and it is also the last loop cable in the list).

1. Make a parent array with every node its own root.
  2. For each cable [a, b], find the roots of a and b.
  3. If the roots are equal, return [a, b].
  4. Otherwise union them.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: For each cable from the end, remove it and check with DFS whether the rest is a connected tree.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Union-find with path compression; one pass over the cables.

explain: For [[1,2],[1,3],[2,3]]: [1,2] joins 1 and 2, [1,3] joins 3 into that set, and [2,3] finds 2 and 3 already together, so [2,3] is the answer. Every cable on the loop would fix the tree, but the cable that closes it while scanning in order is exactly the one that appears last among the loop cables. Labels start at 1, so size the parent array n + 1.
recognize: Edges added one by one and you need the one that first creates a cycle → union-find.
